chapter: Changing styles, the road and nightlife
title: New York after-hours spots: Minton's, Monroe's, White Rose, Beefsteak Charlie's
summary: Saunders recalls where New York musicians jammed and drank.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: There used to be an after-hours place up near the Apollo, wasn't there? A place where guys used to go after they got through work?
Well, there was a lot of places around New York, where they used to -- yeah, Minton's, you mean, Minton's.
Yeah, Minton's. That was the after hours -- where they jammed and blew and all of that. All the guys would go to Minton's, right.

Yeah, right, uptown, Monroe's uptown, Small's Paradise. All of these clubs were running around New York at that time. And New York was jumping, and then, all of the guys that played at theatres and all that kind of thing all drank downtown, at the White Rose, was a tavern there.
They used to all -- if you wanted to find anybody, go to the White Rose and you could catch them. They served great big shots.
Yeah. I think they're still in existence. Don Byas did a tune in the mid-'40s, called 'White Rose Kick.'
Right. But that was -- the White Rose, and then they had another called Beefsteak Charlie's. And this is still -- I think it's on around 57th Street. I'm not positive.

Beefsteak Charlie's. They'd go in there and every Monday they'd have a little cold cuts and things, and this was a meeting place for a lot of musicians and the performers and everything. And I was there in 1968 the last time I was in New York, and they were still going. You'd go in and--
Yeah, there was always a musician's hangout in New York.
I wish there still was in Chicago.
